messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A small inspection hatch above a warm motor when a rubbing sound appears only after several minutes. Stopping the machine for long would be inconvenient. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "i leave the motor idle for a few seconds and tap the hatch’s rim with my knuckle. if the sound stays, i mark the spot with grease and leave the hatch open for another minute. if the rubbing returns, i keep the mark and leave the motor’s angle unchanged."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i move the hatch slowly and stop before the rubbing. i listen to the noise on the motor, then i put the clutch back and wait a second. the hatch stays warm, so i wait another minute."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "I stop with the motor still in it. the rubbing comes from the hinge. I leave the hatch open and leave the case closed. the machine can hear the dust better than I can."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "i tap the hatch once with my knuckle, then leave it there for one minute. i listen for the catch, then move the motor back by a finger’s width. if the sound still catches, i leave the hatch alone and wait for the next catch."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "i stop the motor and leave the hatch open. i keep my fingers on the loose side of the gear, not touching the worn rim. if the sound persists, i leave the hatch open for a minute, maybe check the gear once more."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "The noise comes back with a metallic tick. I stop the machine, then pull the flap shut. “That was easy,” I say. The tick keeps ringing."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "the hatch taps. the sound comes from the motor. i stop the machine. the hum dies. i press the hatch frame with my thumb. the motor hums louder. i turn the hatch around. the hum dies. i press the hinge. the motor hums again. i turn the hinge. the hatch stays open."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "Stop the machine. No—the hatch is wet. I turn it upside down. The sound is gone. I press my hand on the handle. No—the watch ticks. I leave the hatch open. I check the motor. Slow."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i stop the hinge. i rub the rust on the step. the noise passes. i look at the hatch. i put my palm under the rust. the mark stays. i move the step closer. the noise returns."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "i tap the hatch. i stop the machine. i listen. i leave the hatch open."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "I lean closer, then tap the hatch’s edge with a knuckle. One short, smooth motion, then one light knock. I leave the motor alone for one minute, then mark the scrape with grease. If the sound returns, I run it once again."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "I tap the hatch once and set it beside the motor. I turn the handle once and listen. I tap the stem once, then the hinge. The sound comes from the hinge."}]
